# CLI reference

# CLI reference

This page holds the output of `odctl --help` and of `odctl <command> --help`, captured when the site was built.

## odctl

```text
Usage: odctl [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

 ODCTL CLI - Orchestrator for the Open Data Stack.

 Manage your local data engineering and MLOps infrastructure effortlessly.
 Provides commands to inspect, provision, and tear down curated Docker Compose
 stacks.

╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --install-completion          Install completion for the current shell.      │
│ --show-completion             Show completion for the current shell, to copy │
│                               it or customize the installation.              │
│ --help                        Show this message and exit.                    │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Global Options ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --verbose                    Enable debug-level logging across all commands. │
│ --workspace  -w      <path>  Path to the ODCTL workspace directory (default: │
│                              ./.odctl).                                      │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Inspection & Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ list      List all available profiles and their capabilities.                │
│ explain   Explain the details, services, images, and dependencies of a       │
│           profile.                                                           │
│ ps        List Docker containers managed by the Open Data Stack.             │
│ info      Show the installed odctl version and whether Docker is reachable.  │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Workspace ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ init      Initialize a local .odctl workspace for custom configurations.     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Cluster Lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ pull      Pre-fetch Docker images without starting the containers.           │
│ up        Launch Open Data profiles.                                         │
│ down      Stop and remove profile containers and networks.                   │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Management ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ logs      Fetch the logs of containers managed by specific profiles.         │
│ restart   Restart one or more specific profiles.                             │
│ recreate  Replace one or more profiles' containers, applying compose file    │
│           changes.                                                           │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # View all profiles and exposed ports

   $ odctl list -d


   # See exactly what the kafka-lite profile provisions

   $ odctl explain kafka-lite


   # Launch specific profiles and their dependencies

   $ odctl up flink-lite kafka-lite spark-lite


   # Complete teardown and wipe all data

   $ odctl down --all --volumes
```

## odctl list

```text
Usage: odctl list [OPTIONS]

 List all available profiles and their capabilities.

 A profile is a specific capability or technology (e.g., `kafka-lite`,
 `spark-lite`, `airflow`)
 provided by the Open Data Stack. This command lists them alongside their
 parent stack.

╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --details  -d        Inspect docker-compose files to show exact services and │
│                      exposed host ports.                                     │
│ --help               Show this message and exit.                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # View all basic profiles

   $ odctl list


   # View profiles, underlying services, and ports

   $ odctl list -d
```

## odctl explain

```text
Usage: odctl explain [OPTIONS] {profile}

 Explain the details, services, images, and dependencies of a profile.

 Displays a detailed breakdown of what a profile provisions, its container
 images,
 exposed host ports, and any prerequisite profiles it depends on.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    profile      <str>  The target profile to inspect (e.g., 'airflow',     │
│                          'kafka-lite').                                      │
│                          [required]                                          │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --help          Show this message and exit.                                  │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # See what the Spark profile provisions

   $ odctl explain spark-lite
```

## odctl init

```text
Usage: odctl init [OPTIONS]

 Initialize a local .odctl workspace for custom configurations.

 Copies the bundled docker-compose files, configs, and `.env` template into a
 local `./.odctl/` directory. You can then edit these files directly to
 customize the stack.

╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --force  -f        Wipe out the existing workspace and recreate it from      │
│                    scratch.                                                  │
│ --help             Show this message and exit.                               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # Initialize a new workspace in ./.odctl/

   $ odctl init


   # Recreate workspace, overwriting any local changes

   $ odctl init --force
```

## odctl pull

```text
Usage: odctl pull [OPTIONS] [profiles]...

 Pre-fetch Docker images without starting the containers.

 Useful for downloading heavy images (like Spark, Flink, Kafka) ahead of time
 or ensuring you have the latest versions before launching.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│   profiles      <str>  Specific profiles to pull images for.                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --all   -a        Pull images for ALL available profiles in the registry.    │
│ --help            Show this message and exit.                                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # Pre-fetch images for all profiles

   $ odctl pull --all


   # Pre-fetch images just for Flink and Kafka

   $ odctl pull flink-lite kafka-lite
```

## odctl up

```text
Usage: odctl up [OPTIONS] {profiles}...

 Launch Open Data profiles.

 Resolves dependencies for the requested profiles and brings up the required
 Docker Compose stacks in the correct topological order.

 Refuses to start if the images for the resolved TAG are not published,
 naming the tag rather than leaving Docker to report a missing manifest.
 Warns about any service whose declared profile belongs to another compose
 file, since the planner will never start it.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    profiles      <str>  One or more profiles to launch (e.g., 'ch-lite',   │
│                           'kafka-lite').                                     │
│                           [required]                                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --dry-run          Preview the execution plan without actually starting      │
│                    anything.                                                 │
│ --pull             Force pull the latest images from the registry before     │
│                    starting.                                                 │
│ --help             Show this message and exit.                               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # Launch Clickhouse, Flink, and their dependencies

   $ odctl up ch-lite flink-lite


   # Preview what would be launched for Airflow

   $ odctl up airflow --dry-run


   # Force pull latest images before launching

   $ odctl up kafka-lite --pull
```

## odctl down

```text
Usage: odctl down [OPTIONS] [profiles]...

 Stop and remove profile containers and networks.

 Tears down the requested profiles. Services keep their data inside their
 containers, so the data is removed with them.
 Use --volumes to also remove named volumes, such as the shared jar volume.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│   profiles      <str>  Specific profiles to stop.                            │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --all      -a        Stop ALL running profiles.                              │
│ --volumes  -v        Also remove named volumes, including the shared jar     │
│                      volume once no other profile uses it.                   │
│ --dry-run            Preview the teardown plan without actually stopping     │
│                      anything.                                               │
│ --help               Show this message and exit.                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # Stop specific profile(s)

   $ odctl down kafka-lite


   # Stop all running profiles

   $ odctl down --all


   # Complete teardown and wipe all data

   $ odctl down --all -v
```

```text
 List Docker containers managed by the Open Data Stack.

 Filters out system containers and only shows those belonging to requested
 profiles.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│   profiles      <str>  Specific profiles to inspect.                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --all   -a        Show all containers managed by ODCTL.                      │
│ --help            Show this message and exit.                                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # Show all running containers managed by ODCTL

   $ odctl ps --all


   # Show containers just for specific profiles

   $ odctl ps kafka-lite spark-lite
```

## odctl logs

```text
Usage: odctl logs [OPTIONS] {profiles}...

 Fetch the logs of containers managed by specific profiles.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    profiles      <str>  Profiles to fetch logs for. [required]             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --service     -s      <str>  Filter to a specific compose service (Use       │
│                              'odctl ps' to find names).                      │
│ --follow      -f             Follow log output in real-time.                 │
│ --tail        -n      <str>  Number of lines to show from the end of the     │
│                              logs.                                           │
│                              [default: all]                                  │
│ --timestamps  -t             Show timestamps.                                │
│ --since               <str>  Show logs since timestamp or relative (e.g.     │
│                              '42m').                                         │
│ --until               <str>  Show logs before a timestamp or relative.       │
│ --help                       Show this message and exit.                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:

   # Tail the last 50 lines of all Flink containers and follow live

   $ odctl logs flink-lite -n 50 -f


   # View logs strictly for the JobManager service

   $ odctl logs flink-lite -s jobmanager


   # Show logs with timestamps for the last 10 minutes

   $ odctl logs kafka-lite --since 10m -t
```

# Troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

## Containers exit or Docker runs out of memory

Each service has a memory limit, listed on its [profile page](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/profiles/index.md). The limits of everything you start add up, and Docker needs that much memory available. Give Docker 8 to 16 GB, start fewer profiles at once, or choose a lite profile over a full one. To lower a limit, edit `mem_limit` in the compose file in `.odctl` and run `odctl recreate <profile>`.

## A port is already in use

Every service publishes fixed host ports, listed on its profile page. If another program holds one, `odctl up` fails to start that service. Stop the other program, or change the host side of the port mapping in `.odctl/compose-*.yml` and run `odctl recreate <profile>`. Containers still reach each other on their internal ports, so only clients on your host need the new port.

## Use 127.0.0.1, not localhost

Host addresses in `odctl explain` and on these pages use `127.0.0.1`. With IPv6 enabled in Docker, `localhost` can resolve to a service's IPv6 address, and services that listen on IPv4 only reset the connection. `localhost` works when Docker's IPv6 is off.

## No published image for a TAG

`odctl up` checks the images odctl builds before it starts anything. If the registry says an image for the resolved `TAG` does not exist, it stops with `No published image for TAG=...` and lists the missing images. An image already on your machine passes without a registry call. If the registry cannot be reached, odctl starts anyway and Docker reports what it finds.

The usual causes are a CLI version whose images are not published yet, or a `TAG` in `.odctl/.env` that you changed by hand. Set `TAG` to a published version in `.odctl/.env`, or install a CLI version whose images exist.

## Workspace TAG differs from the CLI version

After you upgrade the CLI, every command except `odctl init` warns that `.odctl/.env` sets an older `TAG`. The workspace keeps the old profiles, images and compose files until you run `odctl init --force`, which also resets your edits.

## A service is up but does not work

`odctl logs <profile>` shows the logs of a profile's containers. Add `-s <service>` for one service, or `-f` to follow them. `odctl ps --all` shows every container odctl manages and its state.
# About

# Roadmap

The work comes in the order shown, without dates: a release ships when it is ready. The timeline marks the work in progress and what follows it: features first, then the testing and setup work that adds no feature. Each planned item links to its GitHub issue.

## Now and next

Localhost-only services

In 1.1.0: every service is reachable from your machine only, and the docs have this Roadmap and a [Changelog](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/about/changelog/index.md).

Streaming

Flink writes to HTTP APIs such as Feast's push endpoint, Spark reads Kafka without downloading packages, and a guide to Kafka retention. [#151](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/151)

Feast

An MCP endpoint for agents, pushing streaming features and materialising from Airflow, and vector retrieval on PostgreSQL. [#150](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/150)

OpenMetadata connectors and Kafka schemas

A Python connector uploaded to S3 is picked up by OpenMetadata, the way the `airflow` profile picks up DAGs, and extra packages can be installed in the ingestion container. Kafka topics whose producers use no schema registry get their fields from JSON Schemas registered in Karapace, with no producer change. [#148](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/148)

Stable interface and JSON output

A written list of what 1.x keeps stable: profile names, ports, `.env` keys, volumes and the workspace files. `--json` on `list`, `explain`, `ps` and `info`, and `--yes` on `init` and `down` for scripts. [#140](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/140)

MCP server

Tools for AI agents that show the profiles and what is running, with `up` and `down` behind a setting. [#141](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/141)

## Later

The work after that, in the order it is planned.

- **Langfuse**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  A profile for tracing and evaluating LLM and agent applications, using odctl's ClickHouse.

  [#120](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/120)

- **desflow server**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  After desflow 1.0, when its server ships: A profile that runs the [desflow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/) simulation server, so a project can start simulations that write to Kafka, PostgreSQL or Iceberg.

  [#144](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/144)

- **Snapshot and restore**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  `odctl snapshot` and `odctl restore` save a profile's data and bring it back, so a lab or an agent can start again from a known state.

  [#142](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/142)

- **Lineage and alerts**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Lineage from Airflow, Spark and Feast in Marquez, and Grafana alert rules, starting with one for a failed DAG run.

  [#149](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/149)

- **Kafka Connect transforms**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Transforms built into the Connect image: make a record schema required, replace personal fields with a hash, and send lineage events to Marquez for any connector.

  [#143](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/143)

- **Testing and CI**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  The end-to-end tests run on every pull request, including image updates, so an update is tested before it merges. Each release is also tested as an upgrade from the one before it, and on arm64, which most Macs run. A pull request then tests only the profiles it changes, and the full suite runs every night.

  [#102](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/102)

- **Memory check**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  `odctl up` warns when Docker has less memory than the profiles it starts need.

  [#155](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/155)

- **Models on the host**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  One setting lets containers reach a model server on the host with an OpenAI-compatible API, such as Ollama or LM Studio, on macOS, Linux and WSL2.

  [#109](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/109)

## Alongside

Work that does not wait for a release, published as it is ready.

- **Labs**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  A series in seven parts that takes one generated dataset of web events and logs through Kafka, Flink, ClickHouse, Spark, Trino and the MLOps tools, each lab listed on the [Labs](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/labs/index.md) page as it is published.

  [benchtop #1](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/benchtop/issues/1)

- **Guides**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Iceberg table maintenance with Spark, vector search in Valkey, and traces and prompts in MLflow.

  [#152](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/152)

# Changelog

Each release, newest first: what changed, then under Upgrading what to change in commands, workspaces or clients that use the previous release. Releases up to 1.0.2 are described on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/releases).

## Version 1.1.0

Every service is now reachable from your machine only, and the docs have a [Roadmap](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/about/roadmap/index.md) and a [Changelog](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/about/changelog/index.md).

- Every published port binds to `127.0.0.1`, on macOS, Linux and WSL2, so other machines on your network cannot reach the services. [How you reach a service](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#how-you-reach-a-service) says how to open a port when you need to.
- Kafka no longer publishes ports 29092, 29093 and 29094, which were listeners for a minikube cluster.
- An odctl skill and `llms.txt` help an AI assistant choose a profile and reach its services. See [Use it with an AI assistant](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/getting-started/#use-it-with-an-ai-assistant).
- Eight guides show in a diagram how data moves between their services, and [How it works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/index.md) shows what `odctl up` checks and the order it starts services in. The end-to-end tests run every command the guides show.
- The tables of `odctl ps` and `odctl explain` draw straight right borders on rows with port mappings.
- `odctl down --help` says what `--volumes` removes.

### Upgrading

- To reach a service from another machine, run `odctl init`, remove `127.0.0.1:` from the service's port line in `.odctl/compose-*.yml`, and run `odctl recreate <profile>`.
- A Kafka client in minikube cannot use `host.minikube.internal:29092` any more. Add a listener for it to the Kafka service in `.odctl/compose-kafka.yml`.
- A workspace made by `odctl init` with an earlier release keeps its old compose files, which publish on all interfaces and include port 29092. Run `odctl init --force` to copy the new files; it replaces your edits.
